distribution.narrative: 殷蕙芬等 (1984) and 黄复生等 (2015) document Fujian. Smith et al. (2020) confirms Fujian and adds Chongqing, Shanxi, and Taiwan. Beaver & Liu (2010) independently supports Taiwan and broad China (SE); the broad regional wording is not converted into provinces.

host_note: Beaver & Liu (2010) describes broad polyphagy across angiosperm and gymnosperm trees but explicitly records Pinus luchuensis in Taiwan. Only that resolved species-level host is promoted.
taxonomy_summary: The current accepted identity is Ambrosiophilus atratus (Eichhoff, 1876).

taxonomic_history.name: Xyleborus collis
taxonomic_history.note: Published name currently treated as a synonym; original-description p. 12.

taxonomic_history.name: Ambrosiophilus atratus
taxonomic_history.note: Current accepted name in the integrated taxonomic backbone.

nomenclature_note: Historical records used Xyleborus atratus and later Ambrosiodmus atratus; Beaver & Liu (2010) discusses transfer from Xyleborus to Ambrosiophilus. Current taxonomy follows the integrated backbone.
